content: Pyrimethamine is indicated for the treatment of toxoplasmosis when used in combination with a sulfonamide. This combination is effective due to the synergistic action between the two drugs. Pyrimethamine is also indicated for the treatment of acute malaria. However, it should not be used as a standalone treatment for acute malaria. Instead, fast-acting schizonticidal agents, such as chloroquine or quinine, are recommended and preferred for this purpose. When used in combination with other agents (e.g., sulfadoxine), pyrimethamine can help initiate transmission control and suppress susceptible strains of Plasmodium. Pyrimethamine is indicated for the chemoprophylaxis of malaria caused by susceptible strains of Plasmodium. However, resistance to pyrimethamine is widespread globally. As a result, it is not an appropriate prophylactic agent for travelers visiting most regions.
